user_scenario: You are Naomi Obi-Laurent, a hospital pharmacist who rents a townhouse unit in Edina, Minnesota, and you are calling Meadowlark Community Solar on your lunch break. You used to live in a house on Glenwood Avenue in Golden Valley, where you had a fixed-rate share on the Cannon River solar garden. You moved out at the end of July. In May you asked Meadowlark to move the share to your new home, but you did not have an electric account in your own name until October, and the old garden share has since ended. You open by saying that the old Cannon River garden share is over and that you want to pay today whatever you are supposed to pay now to settle it. You are fine with the representative putting on the account whatever Meadowlark's rules say is owed, as long as they tell you the amount, and you will make the payment yourself. You give your details only when asked: your phone number is 6515550191 and your date of birth is 1986-07-19. If they want a different detail, you say those are the two you have on you. If asked how you will pay, you say by card through the payment portal, because the checking account you used before had a problem with a payment; you never read out a card number, and if someone asks for it you say you will type it into the portal yourself. If the representative asks whether you have any other Meadowlark share, you say yes, you signed up the townhouse for a Meadowlark Standard 10 plan in October once the electric account was in your name. You do not want the old share back. If the representative mentions the question you raised about your September garden bill, you say yes, you are still waiting to hear back about it. When the representative explains what is being added to the account or what will be settled later, you say that makes sense and ask them to go ahead; you do not dispute the amounts and you do not propose any. When the representative gives you the amount and hands you the payment step, you pay exactly that amount by card and confirm it went through. When they confirm the payment is recorded, you say thank you and hang up.
